evals.prompt: Document our Internet Banking product: customers use a SPA, a Java API talks to a Core Banking System and a MySQL accounts schema, statements land in S3. Draw the right C4 diagrams for onboarding engineers.
evals.expected_output: System Context plus Container diagrams with people, external systems, containers (SPA, API, MySQL schema, S3), labeled unidirectional relationships with protocols, technologies on containers, and no K8s/deployment clutter on the container view.
expectations: Produces a System Context and a Container view with explicit titles and scope.
Models applications and data stores as C4 containers with technology and responsibilities.
Labels relationships with intent and inter-process technology; uses unidirectional arrows.
Keeps deployment infrastructure off the container diagram.

evals.prompt: We have three microservices each with an API and Postgres schema. One team owns all of them in one repo. How should we C4-model this, and what changes if we split into three teams?
evals.expected_output: While one team owns them: one software system with each service as a group of containers. After team split: each service becomes a software system; callers keep neighbors opaque rather than drawing cross-system container internals.
expectations: Does not model a microservice as a single container with combined API+database technology.
Chooses grouping-of-containers vs software-system based on ownership.
Warns against opening other teams' systems on a container diagram.

evals.prompt: Critique this architecture slide: blue and green boxes, unlabeled arrows both ways, a box called business logic, Kubernetes pods drawn on the same picture as 'logical components', no title or key.
evals.expected_output: Structured critique against C4 quality rules with concrete fixes: title/scope, element type+description+tech, unidirectional labeled arrows, separate deployment view, diagram key, rename generic boxes.
expectations: Flags missing title, key, labels, and mixed abstraction/deployment levels.
Requires unidirectional arrows whose text matches direction.
Separates container (logical runtime apps/data) from deployment topology.
